questions.text: Walk me through how you'd handle a dataset with significant class imbalance for a binary classification problem.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Mentions resampling (SMOTE/undersampling), class weights, and choosing metrics like PR-AUC/F1 over accuracy.

questions.text: How would you detect and address multicollinearity in a regression model?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: VIF scores, correlation matrices, dropping or combining features, regularization (Ridge/Lasso).

questions.text: Explain the bias-variance tradeoff and how it shows up when tuning a model.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Underfitting vs overfitting, learning curves, regularization, cross-validation.

questions.text: How do you validate that an A/B test result is statistically significant and not due to chance?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: p-values, confidence intervals, power analysis, multiple-testing correction.

questions.text: Describe your process for feature engineering when working with time-series data.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Lag features, rolling windows, seasonality decomposition, avoiding leakage from future data.

questions.text: Tell me about a time your analysis contradicted a stakeholder's assumption. How did you handle it?
Describe a project where the data was messy or incomplete. How did you move forward?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Pragmatic data cleaning decisions, documenting assumptions, iterative delivery.

questions.text: Tell me about a time you had to explain a complex model to a non-technical audience.
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Simplification without losing accuracy, use of visuals/analogies.

questions.text: Describe a time you disagreed with a teammate's modeling approach. What did you do?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Respectful debate, evidence-based resolution, outcome for the project.

questions.text: Tell me about a project that didn't go as planned. What did you learn?
questions.ideal_answer_notes: Ownership, root-cause reflection, concrete change in future practice.
